<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources targeting prebuilt binary tarballs from the project's GitHub releases, specific to each architecture. The `source` URLs are constructed using the declared `pkgver` and the project URL, pointing to versioned release assets, which is standard practice for binary packages. Checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded files will be verified during the sourcing process.

The PKGBUILD contains no `pkgver()` function, so no dynamic version calculation is performed. The global scope consists only of static variable assignments, with no command substitution, function calls, or external code execution. There is no top-level code that would execute dangerous commands when the PKGBUILD is sourced. The `package()` function is irrelevant for this audit stage due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so it is not evaluated.

Fetching and sourcing this PKGBUILD with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unsafe operations occur during the sourcing phase. The use of static, checksummed sources from the official GitHub repository presents no supply-chain risk at this stage.
</details>
<evidence>

No dynamic or malicious code in sourcing phase</summary>
</security_assessment>

The source URLs are constructed using the `url` variable pointing to `https://github.com/IvelOt/hal-9001`, and the release assets are versioned and match the `pkgver`. The SHA-256 checksums are provided for both architectures and are fixed, not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified integrity.

The `package()` function performs standard operations: installing the binary, creating a symlink, and placing documentation, configuration, and desktop files in appropriate directories. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network access, or unexpected file operations. The use of `install` and `ln` is normal for Arch packages, and all paths are within `$pkgdir`, ensuring no host system modifications occur during build.

Dependencies and optional dependencies are clearly listed and align with typical system utilities for hardware and service management. The package provides aliases and conflicts cleanly. No scripts execute remotely fetched code, and no `eval`, `curl|bash`, or similar anti-patterns are present.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file is a metadata file used by Arch User Repository (AUR) packages to describe the package and its sources. It does not contain executable code. This file defines the package `hal-9001-bin`, a binary release of a Rust-based TUI system control tool, with standard dependencies and optional dependencies for various system services (e.g., NetworkManager, Bluetooth, audio, etc.).

The sources point to GitHub release binaries for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, hosted at the official repository (https://github.com/IvelOt/hal-9001). The URLs are over HTTPS and match the project's declared upstream. The SHA-256 checksums are provided for both binaries, ensuring integrity verification during package installation. There are no signs of obfuscation, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized network access.

The package provides `hal-9001` and `hal9001`, and conflicts with `hal-9001`, which is typical for binary packages replacing source-built versions. Optional dependencies are documented with Portuguese descriptions, which is acceptable localization. No unsafe operations are present in this metadata file.
</details>

</details>
